fullPassage: Scientific developments and technologies in medical practice have brought us enormous progress in the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases. ① The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. ② Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans. ③ A human’s average life expectancy has increased, but relying too much on medicine damages our body system. ④ Vaccines developed in laboratories have contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden of bacterial and viral diseases and have even led to the elimination of poxvirus. ⑤ For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.
title: Progress Against Infectious Diseases
